summary: Regression check after low-risk security/code-quality cleanup (stable React keys in PortalAppointments.jsx & AppointmentQueue.jsx, doc-only useCallback/useMemo comments, test env-var read for demo password). All three logins (patient / admin / physician), role-based routing, logout, patient booking end-to-end, admin Calendar week view + Block Day dialog, and Settings page (Physician Availability, Daily Break, Blocked Days, Vacations, Closures all present) work with NO console errors and NO regressions. 12/12 backend regression tests green.
critical_code_review_comments: After session logout (sessionStorage cleared), directly navigating to /internal/calendar or /portal/home does NOT client-side-redirect to /login — the URL stays on the protected path (page likely renders blank/loading while API returns 401). Not a data-leak because Bearer auth blocks API calls, and after subsequent SPA navigation the login redirect kicks in, but a ProtectedRoute wrapper that unconditionally redirects when no token exists would give a cleaner UX. Not a regression from this cleanup.

Landing route seems to be /login (contains testids brand-logo/current-signin/internal-login) while /signin is the actual email+password form. Slightly confusing naming — worth a short comment in the router.

Case in test_regression_iter13 body-substring checks: Settings page uses ALL-CAPS section headers (WEEKLY AVAILABILITY, DAILY BREAK, BLOCKED DAYS) — future testers should case-fold when asserting section presence.

Portal booking uses appt-calendar day buttons -> appt-time-<HH:MM> -> native <select data-testid=appt-reason> (use select_option, NOT shadcn combobox) -> appt-submit.
